question: Indicate which of the following deficits leads to a glycogenosis:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hexokinase" -> "impaired glucose phosphorylation" -> "reduced glycolysis" -> "unclear glycogen storage impact" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Hexosaminidase" -> "impaired ganglioside degradation" -> "accumulation of gangliosides" -> "Tay-Sachs disease" -> "not related to glycogenosis" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Glucose 6-phosphatase" -> "impaired conversion of glucose-6-phosphate to glucose" -> "accumulation of glycogen in liver" -> "glycogen storage disease type I (Von Gierke's disease)" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Fructokinase" -> "impaired fructose metabolism" -> "fructosuria" -> "not related to glycogenosis" -> 30%
analysis: Glycogenosis, also known as glycogen storage disease, is a group of metabolic disorders caused by enzyme deficiencies affecting glycogen metabolism. Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency is associated with glycogen storage disease type I (von Gierke disease), which is a type of glycogenosis. This enzyme is crucial for the final step of gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis, where glucose 6-phosphate is converted to free glucose. A deficiency in this enzyme leads to the accumulation of glycogen in the liver and kidneys.
